doc.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

chapter: San Diego and the state of jazz
title: Birthplace and growing up in Dallas and San Diego
summary: Born in San Antonio but raised in Dallas, then San Diego from about age six during the war; moved to Los Angeles in the early 1960s and later back.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well you said the night club scene is what you were familiar with when you were growing up. And you were born in San Antonio, is that right? Did you stay there a long time?

No. We really lived in Dallas, my family. But we happened to — my father did a lot of traveling in his work and we were in San Antonio at that particular time for a brief time, I think just a few months. But really Dallas was where we lived. But then when I was about six, five or six we came out here to San Diego, which was during the war, in the Second World War at that time. And so I really am almost a native, not quite, but I grew up here. And then I moved to L.A. in the early ‘60s and lived up there for almost twenty years, and then moved back to San Diego.
